# vercel_projects (Data Source)

Lists all projects visible to the authenticated user in the selected team or personal account. Uses the provider's default team unless team_id is set. All supplied filters must match. Protection filters describe configured settings, not effective access after bypasses or exceptions. Use protection filters for discovery and audits; using them as resource for_each keys can remove resources from configuration after protection changes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Uses the default team configured on the provider.
data "vercel_projects" "nextjs" {
  framework = "nextjs"
}

output "nextjs_project_ids" {
  value = keys(data.vercel_projects.nextjs.projects)
}

# An explicit team_id overrides the provider's default team.
# Protection filters are useful for audits. Avoid using a changing protection
# state as the for_each selection for resources that change that protection.
data "vercel_projects" "without_passport" {
  team_id          = "team_example"
  passport_enabled = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `framework` (String) Filter by the exact framework slug, for example nextjs. Omit to include all frameworks and projects without a configured framework.
- `passport_enabled` (Boolean) Filter by whether Passport is configured. Omit to include both enabled and disabled projects.
- `password_protection_enabled` (Boolean) Filter by whether Password Protection is configured. Omit to include both enabled and disabled projects.
- `repository_url` (String) Filter by the connected Git repository URL, for example https://github.com/vercel/next.js. Uses the API's repository URL matching.
- `team_id` (String) The team ID to query. Defaults to the team configured on the provider, or the personal account when no team is configured.
- `trusted_ips_enabled` (Boolean) Filter by whether Trusted IPs is configured. Omit to include both enabled and disabled projects.
- `vercel_authentication_enabled` (Boolean) Filter by whether Vercel Authentication is configured. Omit to include both enabled and disabled projects.

### Read-Only

- `projects` (Attributes Map) Matching projects keyed by their stable project IDs. Only project metadata and protection settings are returned; environment variables, passwords and bypass secrets are excluded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects))

### Nested Schema for `projects`

Read-Only:

- `framework` (String) The configured framework. Null when no framework is configured.
- `git_repository` (Attributes) The connected Git repository. Null when no repository is connected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects--git_repository))
- `id` (String) The project ID.
- `name` (String) The current project name.
- `passport` (Attributes) Passport configuration. Bypasses and exceptions can still allow access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects--passport))
- `password_protection` (Attributes) Password Protection configuration. Bypasses and exceptions can still allow access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects--password_protection))
- `team_id` (String) The owning team ID. Null for a personal project.
- `trusted_ips` (Attributes) Trusted IPs configuration. Bypasses and exceptions can still allow access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects--trusted_ips))
- `vercel_authentication` (Attributes) Vercel Authentication configuration. Bypasses and exceptions can still allow access. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects--vercel_authentication))
